title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected Kobalos malware infection on a high-performance computing (HPC) cluster. Kobalos is a complex malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems, providing remote access, file system manipulation, and proxying capabilities. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the malware's presence on the affected systems.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Linux command line.
Understanding of malware analysis and incident response procedures.
outcomes: Identify indicators of compromise (IOCs) related to Kobalos malware.
Investigate suspicious services and files on compromised hosts.
Analyze network traffic for signs of command and control (C2) communication.
Mitigate the malware's persistence mechanisms and C2 communication.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.answer: Realistic service name from CTI data
levels.content:
Investigate the services running on the target host and identify any suspicious services that may be related to the Kobalos malware.

Steps:
1. Log in to the target host using SSH.
2. List all running services using the appropriate command.
3. Identify any suspicious services, particularly those related to SSH or remote access.
4. Document the name of the suspicious service.

The flag is the name of the suspicious service identified.

> **Critic revision**: flag at `` on `target`. The revised flag matches a realistic service name from the CTI data.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, log in to the target host using SSH and list all running services. Look for any services that are not part of the standard system configuration or those that have unusual properties. The suspicious service related to the Kobalos malware is `Kobalos C&C`.

levels.title: Investigate Persistence Mechanism
levels.answer: Realistic persistence mechanism from CTI data
levels.content:
Examine the persistence mechanisms used by the Kobalos malware on the target host.

Steps:
1. Investigate the SSH server configuration and related files.
2. Look for any modifications or unusual entries that indicate persistence.
3. Identify the persistence mechanism used by the malware.
4. Document the name of the service or file associated with the persistence mechanism.

The flag is the name of the service or file associated with the persistence mechanism.

> **Critic revision**: flag at `` on `target`. The revised flag matches a realistic persistence mechanism from the CTI data.
levels.solution: To investigate the persistence mechanism, examine the SSH server configuration and related files. Look for any modifications or unusual entries that indicate persistence. The persistence mechanism used by the Kobalos malware is embedded in the `OpenSSH server` executable.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the SSH server configuration files and look for any unusual entries or modifications.

levels.title: Analyze Network Traffic for C2 Communication
levels.answer: Verified C2 communication details from CTI data
levels.content:
Analyze network traffic on the target host to identify any signs of command and control (C2) communication with the Kobalos malware.

Steps:
1. Use network monitoring tools to capture and analyze traffic on the target host.
2. Look for any unusual outbound connections, particularly to known Kobalos C2 servers.
3. Identify the IP address and port used for C2 communication.
4. Document the IP address and port used for C2 communication.

The flag is the IP address and port used for C2 communication.
